body:
`plain`/`plain_session` refuse a plain project with "this project has no Gleam code (no gleam.toml)" even when the task's other projects have code; `submit`, `check`, `test` and `delete` at the root do not name `--project`.

1. Keep `read_project`'s `store.lang.is_none() && !language::is_rust` gate (saved during the observed run) and add a regression test for `inspect`, `refs` and `find --project <rust>`.
2. Make plain refusals language-neutral and, in a task run, name the task's projects and `--project <folder>` (reuse `other_projects`/`scope::of_task`).
3. Make `grep` after a miss in a project with graph source say the source is `find`'s, not just "No matches"; keep `grep --in <graph file>`'s existing "use `find`" text. `grep --in` a Rust source path that is symbol-held (e.g. `src/store/submit_tests.rs`) must say "use `find`", not "no such file or folder" (seen in run `a348af56b1f15298`).
4. When `submit` refuses with "imports go through `--imports`", name the block and the missing import; when a rename is refused, say how to keep the id (`submit <name>` replaces and may rename).
5. Tests: root task + Rust project refusal names `--project`; `grep` miss in a Rust project names `find`; `grep --in` a symbol-held `.rs` path names `find`; `submit` import refusal names the block/import; `read_project` reads `inspect`, `refs`, `find`.

Checks: `rust-unit`, `rust-board-tests`, `rust-acceptance`.
title: commands: Rust refusal and routing
